text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Japan's Deputy Foreign Minister has said Tokyo is ready to increase Official Development Assistance (ODA) to Vietnam.
-- Businesses will soon be able to buy foreign currencies two or three months before debt payment deadlines. - - - -
-- The possibility of establishing a U.S-ASEAN Center for Technology Cooperation in Hanoi has been discussed during a two-day visit by a U.S-ASEAN Council (USAC) mission.
-- An eight-member delegation from Burma, led by Lieutenant-General Tun Kyi, Minister of Trade, is scheduled to visit Vietnam from March 25 to April 1.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has asked the Ministry of Justice to promote education about law.
-- 24 defendants charged with involvement in a Hanoi-based crime syndicate will hear final court ruling today. - - - -
-- The Laotian Minister of Public Health began a working visit to Vietnam on March 18.
-- Vice Minister of Defence, Tran Hanh paid a visit to Japan from March 11 to 15. - - - -
-- The winter-spring rice harvest in the Cuu Long River Delta is expected to yield some 1.363 million tonnes, but the summer-autumn crop may be late due to seasonal flooding.
-- The Ministry of Culture and Information has decided to establish an inspection group to check implementation of the domestic press law. - - - -
-- The Prime Minister has decided to establish a State Guiding Committee to oversee development work at international airports in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City.
